about.title: Brisbane Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Brisbane sits in a compact but busy stretch of San Mateo County, wedged between US-101 and the hillside industrial areas along Guadalupe Canyon Parkway. That mix of logistics, warehousing, and commercial traffic means workplace injuries here often involve more than a simple slip or fall — delivery drivers, dockworkers, and site crews frequently share space with outside contractors, equipment operators, and vehicles that don't belong to their employer. In California, workers' compensation usually covers job injuries no matter who's at fault, but it doesn't always tell the whole story. When a subcontractor, property owner, or negligent driver on a road like Bayshore Boulevard contributes to the accident, a separate claim against that third party may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured Brisbane workers with an independent attorney who can look at both sides of the situation and explain your options, free of charge.

whyChoose.title: Why Brisbane Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Third-Party Difference
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your only claim against your employer, but a negligent equipment maker, subcontractor, or driver can still be held separately liable. An attorney can help sort out which path — or both — applies to your situation.

items.title: Protecting You From Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to punish you for reporting a job injury. If you're worried about your job after speaking up, an attorney can explain your protections.

items.title: Watching the Clock on Two Different Deadlines
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, while a third-party injury claim carries its own two-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so getting guidance early matters.

items.question: I was hurt while working near US-101 in Brisbane — is that still a workers' comp case?
items.answer: It can be, since workers' comp generally applies regardless of fault if you were injured on the job. But if another driver on US-101 or Bayshore Boulevard caused the crash, there may also be a separate third-party claim worth exploring. An independent attorney can look at the details and explain how both might work together.

items.question: Can I get in trouble with my employer for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No. California law prohibits retaliation against employees who report workplace injuries in good faith. If you're facing pushback or fear losing your job, that's worth discussing with an attorney right away.

items.question: What if my injury involved a subcontractor or someone from a different company?
items.answer: That's fairly common on multi-employer job sites, especially around Brisbane's warehouse and logistics areas. When someone outside your own employer contributes to your injury, you may have a claim against that third party in addition to your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who can evaluate both.
